Background (from the session that started this one):
Kenneth is building a 3-step "Add a printer" form in JusPrin's printer chat (a fork of OrcaSlicer). Its brand, model and nozzle lists come from the existing PrinterCatalog, which reads all packaged vendor profiles. Kenneth remembers this being costly enough to lock the UI for a few seconds and wants that checked before the form ships. The form itself is being built in a separate worktree (.claude/worktrees/add-printer-popup, uncommitted); do not edit that worktree. This investigation is independent of it: the catalogue code is the same on jusprin-newui.

Task:
Find out whether building JusPrin's printer catalogue blocks the UI for seconds, and if it does, propose how to fix it. Report to Kenneth and get his agreement before changing any code.

What to investigate (repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin, branch jusprin-newui):
1. `PrinterCatalog::load` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp:98) walks every vendor index in `resources/profiles/*.json` (64 brands, 383 models, about 987 model+nozzle variants), parses each vendor's machine JSON files and resolves their `inherits` chains. That is thousands of small JSON reads. `panel_printers()` then folds the variants into models.
2. Find every caller and when it runs, and on which thread. Known caller: the `PrinterPanel` constructor (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp:51, `PrinterCatalog::load(Slic3r::resources_dir())`). Is `PrinterPanel` built once at shell startup, or every time the printer panel opens (Home's "+ Add printer", "Printer settings…")? Grep for other callers too (Home, the shell harness, MCP printer tools).
3. Measure it, on this Mac, cold (first read after a reboot is impossible; use a fresh process and also purge the file cache only if that needs no password) and warm. A small timing around the call in a build, or a tiny test binary, is fine. Report milliseconds, not impressions. The machine is often heavily loaded by other sessions' builds (load average 30-40): record `uptime` alongside each measurement, and repeat a few times.
4. If it is slow enough to notice (say over ~100 ms on the GUI thread), propose fixes and recommend one. Candidates to weigh: build the catalogue once and share it; load it on a worker thread and let the panel show a loading state; reuse what OrcaSlicer already parsed (`PresetBundle::load_system_models_from_json`, VendorProfile models); generate a compact index at build time (the build already has a `jusprin_catalogs` target, check what it produces). Say what each costs and what it risks.

Rules (from agent-docs/jusprin/README.md, fork-stewardship.md and AGENTS.md):
- Attribute behaviour correctly: "OrcaSlicer does X" only for upstream code; check with `git show 3ffb9585d2:<path>` (upstream merge base) or git blame.
- Label anything inferred as inference. Measure before claiming.
- Do not apply a fix you have not shown to be needed. Stop after the report and ask Kenneth, with each decision written out in full as a question with options, consequences and your recommendation.
- No live AI model calls. Commit nothing unless Kenneth asks.
- Never drive another JusPrin instance; Kenneth may have one open. If you run the app or the shell harness, use an isolated data dir (the shell harness makes its own).
- Build recipe for a worktree: see /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md (use /Applications/CMake.app cmake, the llvm-ar flags on a fresh build dir, absolute build paths; `--config Release` saves disk). Wait on a background build by its PID with `kill -0`, not `pgrep -f` (that matches its own loop).

Done means: a short plain-English report (problem, measurements with numbers, cause, recommended fix and alternatives, open questions for Kenneth) and no code changes yet.

## Where and when it runs

- App path: MainFrame::MainFrame (MainFrame.cpp:541) -> JusPrin::attach_shell -> ShellController::install
  (ShellController.cpp:529) -> new PrinterPanel -> PrinterCatalog::load (PrinterPanel.cpp:51), then
  OrcaPrinterBackend's constructor calls panel_printers() once (OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:49).
- Once per launch, on the GUI thread, before the main window is shown. All fork code (the
  attach_shell line is on no upstream branch).
- The PrinterPanel lives as long as the shell does. Home "+ Add printer", "Printer settings…", Connect and
  filament help all call PrinterPanel::open / open_filament, which rebuild the web view but do NOT reload
  the catalogue.
- Other callers: tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp (6 call sites, test-only) and
  tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:1990.
- History: from 39c077bff8 (2026-09-13) to 0e55c4f9be (2026-09-17), show_printer_setup() loaded the
  catalogue on every opening of the old "Add a printer" modal.
- The add-printer-popup worktree (uncommitted, read only) adds no new PrinterCatalog::load callers.
- `jusprin_catalogs` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/catalogs.cmake) builds translation .mo files, not printer data.
- Upstream startup (PresetBundle::load_system_presets_from_json) reads data_dir/system, i.e. installed vendors
  only. load_system_models_from_json (upstream, used by CreatePresetsDialog) reads every vendor's index and
  model files with LoadVendorOnly; it does not read the machine presets the catalogue needs for build
  volume, nozzle-variant preset names and the default filament.

## Measurements

Probe: the unmodified PrinterCatalog.cpp compiled alone with clang++ -O2 (same flags level as
RelWithDebInfo) and the repo's deps_src/nlohmann, run in fresh processes on an Apple M2 Pro (12 cores).
Sources in the session scratchpad (bench/main.cpp, bench/instr.cpp).

Output: 987 variants, 383 models, 64 brands; 1,608 files read, 4.8 MB of JSON.

| Condition | load() ms | load average |
|---|---|---|
| First run on this checkout's files | 535 | 4.5 |
| Repo files, fresh processes | 231, 190, 211, 204 | 4.5 |
| Repo files, 5 loads in one process | 220, 188, 150, 189, 192 | 4.5 |
| Uncached APFS clone of profiles/ (approximates a cold read; `purge` needs a password) | 313, 327, 323, 319 | 5.2 |
| Same clone, second run | 130, 129, 129 | 5.2 |
| Repo files, 36 busy loops on 12 cores | 521, 353, 386, 460 | 8 -> 16 |

panel_printers(): 0.42–0.57 ms every time.

Breakdown (instrumented copy, cached files, ~141 ms total): file open+read 45 ms, JSON parse 31 ms,
inherits resolution 39 ms, artwork exists() 2 ms. Uncached: file open+read 222 ms of 319.
Under CPU contention inherits resolution grew to 190–210 ms: resolve_machine copies every ancestor's JSON
object at each level and runs twice per machine (once to map model+nozzle to preset, once per variant).

## Options weighed

1. Leave it. Cost stays at launch only.
2. Make load() cheaper in place (fork file only): resolve each machine once and reuse it, skip the second
   resolve pass. Expected to remove most of the 39 ms (or 200 ms under contention); unmeasured.
3. Start load() on a worker thread at launch; PrinterPanel waits for it at first open. Removes the whole
   cost from launch; adds a future/wait and an error path in the panel.
4. Generate a compact index at build time. Fastest at runtime; adds a build step on 3 platforms and a
   second source of truth for profiles.
5. Reuse PresetBundle/VendorProfile: not a fit, see above.

content.text:
Building the printer catalogue does not lock the UI for seconds, and opening the printer panel never triggers it. The catalogue is built once per app launch, on the GUI thread, before the main window appears. It takes 130–230 ms when the profile files are already in memory and 320–520 ms when they have to be read from disk or the CPUs are busy. I changed no code. The full notes are in `printer-catalog-load-cost.md` in the shared notes folder.

**When it runs**
- The call chain is `MainFrame` constructor → `attach_shell` → `ShellController::install` ([ShellController.cpp:529](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:529)) → `new PrinterPanel` → `PrinterCatalog::load` ([PrinterPanel.cpp:51](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp:51)). All of it is JusPrin code; no upstream OrcaSlicer branch contains the `attach_shell` call.
- The printer panel stays alive as long as the app does. Home's "+ Add printer", "Printer settings…", Connect and filament help each rebuild the panel's web view but reuse the catalogue already loaded.
- Folding the nozzle variants into models (`panel_printers()`) happens once at startup and takes about 0.5 ms.
- The only other callers are in the shell test harness and the unit tests.
- From 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-17 (commit 39c077bff8 up to 0e55c4f9be), the old "Add a printer" dialog did reload the catalogue every time it opened. That is a likely source of the freeze Kenneth remembers, though I haven't confirmed it.
- The uncommitted form in the `add-printer-popup` worktree adds no new calls to the catalogue loader.

**Measurements**

I compiled the unmodified `PrinterCatalog.cpp` on its own at -O2 and ran it in fresh processes on the M2 Pro. It reads 1,608 files (4.8 MB of JSON) and finds 64 brands, 383 models and 987 model-and-nozzle variants.

| Condition | Load time | Load average |
|---|---|---|
| Files already in memory | 130–230 ms | 4.5–5 |
| First read of this checkout's files | 535 ms | 4.5 |
| Uncached copy of the profiles folder (stands in for a cold start) | 313–327 ms | 5.2 |
| All 12 CPU cores kept busy | 353–521 ms | 8–16 |

The machine was lightly loaded during these runs, not at the 30–40 load average it often has. A true cold start after a reboot needs `sudo purge`, which I couldn't run.

**Where the time goes** (about 141 ms in total, files in memory):
- Opening and reading files: 45 ms.
- Parsing JSON: 31 ms.
- Resolving each profile's `inherits` chain: 39 ms. This part grows to about 200 ms when the CPUs are busy, because the code copies every parent profile's JSON at each level and resolves every machine twice.

**Options and recommendation**

I recommend shipping the form with catalogue loading unchanged. The form should take its lists from the existing printer backend, which already holds the folded models, and never reload the catalogue.

If the startup cost matters, these are the alternatives:
1. **Resolve each profile once and reuse it.** This touches only `PrinterCatalog.cpp`, which is a JusPrin file. My estimate, not measured, is that it removes most of the 39 ms, and more on a busy machine.
2. **Load on a worker thread at launch, and have the panel wait at first open.** This takes the whole cost out of startup, but adds threading, a wait, and an error path inside the panel.
3. **Generate a compact index at build time.** This is the fastest at runtime, but it adds a build step on three platforms and a second copy of the profile data to keep in sync. The existing `jusprin_catalogs` build target only builds translation files, so it doesn't help here.
4. **Reuse what OrcaSlicer already parsed.** This doesn't work. OrcaSlicer's startup only loads the vendors the user has installed. Its all-vendor model loader skips the machine profiles the catalogue needs for build volume, the nozzle variants' preset names and the default filament.

**Decisions for Kenneth**
1. **Ship the form without changing how the catalogue loads?**
   - Yes (my recommendation): this adds no risk, and the cost only applies at launch.
   - No, fix it first: this delays the form for a startup saving of 130–520 ms.
2. **Do anything about the startup cost?**
   - Leave it (my recommendation for now).
   - Option 1: a small, low-risk change in one JusPrin file.
   - Option 2: the biggest saving, but it adds threading.
   - Option 3: the most work, and it adds a build step.

Build this worktree in the configuration I actually run (RelWithDebInfo, and also Debug if that’s what my dev build is). Add temporary timing logs around PrinterCatalog::load (PrinterPanel.cpp:51), PrinterPanel::open, and build_runtime(). Launch the real app with an isolated --datadir, and don’t touch my running instance. Record the wall-clock time from launch to the window appearing. Then open Home’s “+ Add printer” and “Printer settings…” three times each, and report every logged time in milliseconds with uptime beside it. metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

In Kenneth's real RelWithDebInfo build, building the printer catalogue blocks the GUI thread for about 0.95 s, once per launch, before the window appears. Opening the printer panel never freezes the UI: each "+ Add printer" or "Printer settings…" opening took 48–82 ms on the GUI thread. The timing logs are removed and nothing was committed.

**Correction to my first report:** RelWithDebInfo compiles at `-O0` on Clang (the root `CMakeLists.txt` replaces `-O2`). My earlier 130–230 ms came from an optimised build and understated Kenneth's dev build about six times.

**How I ran it**
- **Build:** this worktree's RelWithDebInfo, which is Kenneth's dev configuration; the main checkout's Debug folder holds no app. I turned debug info off (`-O0 -g0`) because the disk had 16 GB free and a build with debug info needs about 14 GB. The optimisation level matches Kenneth's `-O0 -g`, so the timings should too.
- **App:** a copy of the app with its own bundle id and an isolated `--datadir` (a scratch copy of Kenneth's JusPrin2 folder). Kenneth's running instance (pid 6888) was not touched.
- **No live model calls:** run 1 had the API keys blanked. Run 2 had placeholder keys, with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` pointed at a closed local port so no request could leave the machine.
- **Window appearing:** a small tool polled the window list for the app's first window at least 900 px wide.

**Launches**

| Launch | Load average | Launch to window | `PrinterCatalog::load` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17.2 | 17,323 ms | 975 ms |
| 2 | 3.5 | 12,219 ms | 934 ms |
| 3 | 4.0 | 11,904 ms | 926 ms |
| 4 (CPUs deliberately saturated) | 18 → 42 | 17,216 ms | 965 ms |

The catalogue is 5–8% of the time to the window, and it finishes about 0.7 s before the window shows.

**Panel openings** (load average 3.4–4.2; each value is `open()` total / `build_runtime`)

| | No agent configured | Agent configured |
|---|---|---|
| "+ Add printer" | 82.4 / 80.4, 53.4 / 53.1, 48.5 / 48.2 ms | 51.7 / 51.3, 50.1 / 49.8, 54.5 / 54.3 ms |
| "Printer settings…" | 48.2 / 47.9, 49.8 / 49.5, 50.4 / 50.1 ms | 52.9 / 52.5, 50.5 / 50.2, 54.6 / 54.2 ms |

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

Running the app
- Use an isolated data directory, for example C:\catalog-timing\datadir, and launch with: orca-slicer.exe --datadir C:\catalog-timing\datadir
- This VM has no GPU. Use the app's Mesa hook (<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll) and set GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe and LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 in the launching environment. Software rendering inflates launch time; the catalogue load is CPU-only, so it is still comparable.
- Anything that touches windows must run in the interactive desktop session (a scheduled task with -LogonType Interactive, or from inside the RDP/console session). Over SSH, window enumeration sees nothing.
- No live AI model calls, ever.
  - Runs "no agent": the data directory has no API keys.
  - Runs "agent configured": with the app closed, edit <datadir>\JusPrin2.conf so its "jusprin_agent" section has provider "openai", openai_api_key "sk-placeholder-not-a-real-key", enabled true, cloud_consent true. Launch with JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9 in the environment, so any request goes to a closed local port.
- The first launch with a fresh data directory shows OrcaSlicer's setup wizard. Finish it, then make sure Home's PRINTERS column shows at least one printer card. If none appears, add one through "+ Add printer" -> "Browse the full printer list" (any printer, 0.4 mm nozzle). Note which log lines came from this setup and exclude them from the results.

What to measure
For every measurement, record the machine load beside it: CPU % (Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select LoadPercentage) and processor queue length (Get-Counter '\System\Processor Queue Length'). Make sure no build or other heavy job is running on the VM during measurements, and say if one was.

1. Launch to window: four separate launches (quit the app in between).
   - Record launch time as Unix epoch ms just before starting the exe.
   - Record when the main window first becomes visible: poll the process's visible top-level windows (EnumWindows + IsWindowVisible + GetWindowRect via Add-Type) every ~20 ms. Count the first window at least 900 px wide, which skips the splash screen.
   - Report launch_to_window_ms, and the PrinterCatalog::load line from the log for that launch.
   - Run launches 1-3 with the agent configured. Run launch 4 with the CPU saturated (start 2x the core count of busy-loop processes 5 s before launch; stop them after the window appears).
2. Panel openings, in one running instance:
   - Three times: Home -> "+ Add printer", wait about 4 s, then "Back".
   - Three times: Home -> a printer card's "…" menu -> "Printer settings…", wait about 4 s, then "Back".
   - Do this once with "no agent" and once with "agent configured" (12 openings in total).
   - For each opening, report the PrinterPanel::open(...) and PrinterPanel::build_runtime ms from the log, and whether the UI visibly froze (an unresponsive window, a "Not responding" title, or a busy cursor). Note what the panel showed: a "No agent connected" page or the printer chat.

Cleanup
- git checkout -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp, and confirm git status shows no changes.
- Quit the app. Delete only the data directory you created, and only after you've copied catalog_timing.log into your report.
- Leave the build directory in place unless disk is short, and report its size and free disk space.

Report (plain English, numbers in milliseconds)
- Machine: VM type, CPU, cores, RAM; build configuration and the exact flags used to compile PrinterPanel.cpp and PrinterCatalog.cpp (/O2 or /Od, /RTC1 or not).
- A table of the four launches: load at launch, launch_to_window_ms, PrinterCatalog::load ms.
- A table of the 12 openings: mode (no agent / agent configured), add or settings, open ms, build_runtime ms, load, froze yes/no.
- Did anything take noticeably longer than on the Mac (load about 0.95 s; open about 50 ms)? If so, which call, and by how much.
- The raw contents of catalog_timing.log.
- Anything you couldn't do or had to change from these instructions, and why.
